item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: Regular hexagon PQRSTU]

PQRSTU is a regular hexagon. What is the measure of the angle QUS?
item.figure_description: A regular hexagon with vertices labeled clockwise: P at the top left, Q at the top right, R at the far right, S at the bottom right, T at the bottom left, and U at the far left. Segment PQ forms the top horizontal edge, and segment TS forms the bottom horizontal edge. Two internal straight line segments are drawn: one connecting vertex U to vertex Q, and another connecting vertex U to vertex S, forming angle QUS.

reference_items.figure_description: A symmetric five-sided polygon ABCDE with a vertical dashed line of symmetry labeled m, which has arrows at both top and bottom ends. The horizontal top side connects vertex A on the left to vertex E on the right, bisected perpendicularly by line m. The left side goes down and outward from A to vertex B, then slants down and inward to vertex C at the bottom, which lies on line m. The right side is a mirror image, going from E down and outward to vertex D, then down and inward to vertex C. Inside the polygon, angle A is marked with an arc and labeled 130, angle B is marked with an arc and labeled 110, and the angle between side BC and line of symmetry m at vertex C is marked with an arc and labeled 30.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Which angle in the figure has a measure closest to 45°?

[Image: Circle divided into angles p, q, r, and s]
reference_items.figure_description: A circle contains a vertical diameter dividing it into left and right halves. From the center, two additional line segments (radii) are drawn: one extending to the left edge at roughly 9 o'clock (slightly below horizontal), and another extending down and to the right at approximately a 45-degree angle from the vertical. Four central angles are labeled: angle q is in the upper-left quadrant (between the upward vertical radius and the left radius, roughly 90°); angle p is in the lower-left quadrant (between the left radius and the downward vertical radius, roughly 90°); angle r is in the upper-right (between the upward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, an obtuse angle of roughly 135°); and angle s is in the lower-right (between the downward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, roughly 45°).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

The triangles shown are congruent. The measures of some of the sides and angles are given. What is the value of x?

The left triangle has a horizontal bottom side. Its left side is labeled "6 cm". The interior angle at the bottom-left vertex is labeled "49°", and the interior angle at the top vertex is labeled "81°".
The right triangle has a nearly horizontal bottom side that slopes slightly downward from right to left, labeled "6 cm". The interior angle at the bottom-right vertex is labeled "81°", and the interior angle at the top vertex is labeled "x°".

reference_items.stem:
In this figure, triangles ABC and DEF are congruent with BC = EF .

What is the measure of angle EGC ?

Segment BC is the base of triangle ABC, and segment EF is the base of triangle DEF. Vertex A is above the baseline, and vertex D is to the right of A and also above the baseline. Side AC intersects side DE at point G. Angle B is labeled 40°, and angle F is labeled 60°.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
